title: How to engage key opinion leaders: an HCP engagement strategy that works
overview: How to engage key opinion leaders and HCPs: a practical HCP engagement strategy for medtech, from peer-to-peer content to physician testimonial video.
author: Made Clear
body:
Knowing how to engage key opinion leaders is one of the most valuable skills a medtech marketing or medical affairs team can have. The physicians who lead the field are also the hardest to reach: their diaries are full, they get asked constantly, and they guard their reputation carefully. The companies that build lasting relationships with them treat engagement as a partnership, not a transaction.

This guide covers what we've learned from years of filming and working with interventional cardiologists and other clinical leaders.

Start with what matters to them

KOLs say yes to projects that advance their field, help their patients and reflect well on their work. Before you ask for their time, be clear about the clinical question the content answers and why their voice is the right one. A request framed around education is far more likely to land than one framed around a product.

On The Radiation Problem, made with Egg Medical and Optima Education, we researched and approached interventional cardiologists who could explain both the science of scatter radiation and its emotional impact on them and their colleagues. Seven of the top interventional cardiologists in the US and UK took part, because the subject mattered to them personally.

Build an HCP engagement strategy, not a one-off shoot

An HCP engagement strategy maps who you need to reach, what they need to hear and who they will listen to. It should answer:

  • Audiences: which physicians, nurses, technologists or hospital decision-makers you need to influence. They often need different messages.
  • Voices: which KOLs each audience trusts, from global names to respected local operators.
  • Formats: interviews, case presentations, education programmes, documentaries or live events.
  • Moments: trial results, congresses, product launches and the long stretches in between.
  • Channels: where each audience will actually see the content.

For Medtronic's HTN:RDN campaign, that meant a two-year programme in phases: a four-part documentary to retell the story of renal denervation, live coverage of pivotal trial results at ACC, a sustained expert-led education programme, and local versions in six languages.

Peer to peer marketing in healthcare

Physicians learn most from other physicians. Peer to peer marketing in healthcare puts KOLs in front of their colleagues to share technique, cases and experience. It works best when it feels like a conversation between equals rather than a presentation.

The Calcium Masterclass is a good example: a high-quality peer-to-peer programme with a faculty from Europe and the US, covering everything from calcium basics to complex cases. Over 5,500 cardiologists took part, spending an average of 28 minutes each.

Making a physician testimonial video that convinces

A physician testimonial video can be the most persuasive piece of content you own, or the least, depending on how it's made. The ones that work share a few traits:

  • Real experience, not a script. Ask about specific cases and decisions, and let the physician answer in their own words.
  • Context. Film in or near the cath lab where possible. For Philips ICE in the Heart, we filmed two leading interventional cardiologists performing the LAAO procedure in their own cath labs, then paired the footage with concise interviews on the device's benefits.
  • Honesty. Physicians spot overclaiming instantly. Balanced, evidence-led answers carry more weight.
  • Brevity. One clear point per film. Cut longer interviews into a series.

Respect their time

The fastest way to lose a KOL is to waste their time. Agree questions in advance, keep shoots tight and schedule around their clinical and congress commitments. Major congresses are ideal: KOLs are already there, often with an hour between sessions. At TCT 2026 we ran an always-on filming booth on Shockwave Medical's stand, capturing KOLs, physicians and leadership in single and two-person interviews throughout the congress.

Keep the relationship going

  • Share the finished content with them first, and make it easy for them to use it in their own teaching.
  • Tell them how it performed and what physicians said.
  • Bring them back for the next chapter, rather than starting from scratch with someone new.
  • Widen the circle over time, so your message isn't carried by a single voice.

Where to begin

Pick one clinical question, two or three trusted voices and one moment, such as a congress or a data release, and build from there. If you'd like to plan your HCP engagement strategy with us, see our KOL content work or get in touch.
